claims.text: The target material is the refractory high-entropy alloy HfNbTaTiZr containing 1 wt.% oxygen.
Molecular dynamics with machine-learning-based force fields can accurately predict the lattice thermal conductivity of HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed simulation predicts lattice heat transport without conflating it with electronic heat transport.
The proposed approach is applicable below 200 K and from 300 to 1200 K.
Lattice distortions and chemical complexity are relevant structural features of HfNbTaTiZr.
Lattice distortions and chemical complexity affect lattice thermal conductivity in HfNbTaTiZr.
Machine-learning-based force fields can capture the effects of lattice distortions and chemical complexity on lattice thermal conductivity.
The lattice thermal conductivity of HfNbTaTiZr will be below 10 W/(K m) at temperatures below 200 K.
The lattice thermal conductivity of HfNbTaTiZr will be above 10 W/(K m) at temperatures above 300 K.
The total thermal conductivity of the oxygen-containing material is 10–17 W/(K m) from 300 to 1200 K.
Prediction accuracy depends on the quality of the machine-learning force field.
Prediction accuracy depends on the complexity of lattice distortions and chemical disorder in the alloy.
Experimental lattice-thermal-conductivity measurements can be compared with the simulation predictions to test the hypothesis.
A significant deviation between measured and predicted lattice thermal conductivity would falsify the hypothesis.
